situation (example wording): "Houston vehicle burglaries where a firearm was stolen, by clearance status" (a NIBRS clearance count or breakdown)
what the app does today: NIBRS clearances are refused in the slice (P57 left the NIBRS method open).
proposed behavior: Method A: count the period's incidents that are cleared as of the latest file, by arrest (the first arrestee segment) or by exceptional clearance, whenever cleared. Clearance is incident-level, per the NIBRS rules: every offense in a cleared incident is cleared. "By clearance status" breaks down into cleared by arrest, cleared exceptionally (with its type) and not cleared. The answer says it counts that period's crimes cleared as of the file date, which is not the FBI's annual method. Historical Part I clearance rates still come from the Crime Index clearances data (P57); state clearance rates stay declined (P18).
exact default or choices offered: Clearance: the period's crimes cleared as of the file date (arrest or exceptional), incident-level; statement: not the FBI's annual method.
why: One rule for every NIBRS clearance answer, said plainly; the annual method stays with the historical figures.
status: Decided 2026-10-30 (Jeff: "Agreed on A"); the unit and levels are refined by P66
